ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Wheat straw dominant (highest energy contribution). Barley, hazelnut shells, cotton stalks, sunflower straw, olive prunings also significant. Some residues (hazelnut) already exported as biomass pellets.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: FAO FRA 2020 Turkey; calc: roundwood ~22 Mm3/yr × 25% residue × 0.45 t/m3; plantation sector growing
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Significant plantation forestry (black pine, eucalyptus). Logging residues concentrated in Black Sea and Aegean regions.

msw_total_mt.source: EEA Turkey municipal waste factsheet 2025; Wikipedia Turkey waste management; ~30 Mt/yr figure cited widely for recent years
msw_total_mt.notes: ~81% landfill (2021 EEA); <1% WtE; ~17% recycling/composting. Turkey has goal to expand WtE.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: ScienceDirect pii/S0921344919300928: Turkey MSW composition studies; organic ~30% + paper ~12% + textiles ~5% = ~47–60% biogenic
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Middle-income country; transitional composition

msw_treatment.source: EEA Turkey municipal waste factsheet 2025; ScienceDirect pii/S0921344919300928

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: FAO 2022 cattle ~17M + sheep ~43M + goats ~11M + poultry ~330M; standard excretion factors × 12% DM; PMC10998781
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large sheep herd mostly pastoral. Cattle and poultry have some concentrated systems.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 85M pop × ~60% treatment × 25 g DS/person/day × 365 / 1e9
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Improving WWTP coverage; Istanbul well-served

nutrient_status_source: FAO; central Anatolian plateau moderate; coastal regions higher input
notes: Good governance, EU candidate status provides regulatory alignment. Significant biomass resource with existing biomass pellet export sector (hazelnut to EU). Strong candidate for Frontier scouting. Wheat belt in Central Anatolia and Black Sea region hazelnut zone offer concentrated collection points.

name: Saudi Arabia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Springer doi:10.1007/s13369-025-10976-3; calc: FAOSTAT 2022 wheat ~1 Mt + dates ~1.7 Mt (fronds/pits) + vegetables + alfalfa × RPR × 30% recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Date palm fronds significant but diffuse. Wheat straw from Madinah/Qassim region. Very limited ag sector overall (desert nation, water-constrained).

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: FAO FRA 2020; essentially no commercial forest
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Desert nation — negligible forestry

msw_total_mt.source: EcoMENA; multiple reviews citing ~15–16 Mt at 1.39 kg/cap/day × ~32M pop (2017); article:10.1177/0734242X211068236
msw_total_mt.notes: ~65% to sanitary landfill; ~25% open dump; ~8% recycling; WtE emerging (Jeddah pilots). Organic fraction ~40%.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EcoMENA; Saudi MSW: organic ~40% + paper ~20% = ~60%; adjusted for dry weight to 0.55

msw_treatment.source: EcoMENA; article 10.1177/0734242X211068236; Saudi Vision 2030 waste targets

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: FAO 2022 sheep ~9M + goats ~4M + cattle ~0.5M + camels ~0.5M + poultry ~200M; standard excretion factors
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large industrial poultry sector (Al-Watania, Fakieh) concentrated in Riyadh/Jeddah regions.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 35M pop × ~60% treatment × 25 g DS/person/day × 365 / 1e9
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: High urban coverage; rural areas minimal

nutrient_status_source: FAO; desert soils; very low organic matter
notes: Biomass resource very limited for a large economy. MSW and poultry manure are best concentrated feedstocks. Saudi Vision 2030 includes waste-to-energy ambitions. Governance: strong state capacity but autocratic. Climate-aligned investment interest growing. No domestic storage options known — CCS would require offshore or EOR in oilfields.

name: Iran

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: ScienceDirect pii/S1364032113001731: total agricultural residues ~25–28 Mt/yr range for Iran; Khuzestan province alone 5.5 Mt theoretical; calc: FAOSTAT 2022 wheat ~13 Mt + rice ~2 Mt + sugarcane ~7 Mt + barley + cotton × RPR × 30% recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Wheat straw dominant (Khuzestan, Isfahan, Khorasan). Rice straw (Caspian coast). Sugarcane bagasse in Khuzestan concentrated at mills. Significant open burning of rice straw.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: FAO FRA 2020 Iran; calc: Hyrcanian forests + plantation sector; roundwood ~4 Mm3/yr
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Hyrcanian forests (UNESCO) — sourcing from there must be excluded. Commercial plantation forestry modest.

msw_total_mt.source: EcoMENA Middle East waste data; calc: 87M pop × 0.57 kg/cap/day; Tehran alone ~4 Mt/yr
msw_total_mt.notes: Mix of sanitary landfill and open dump. Tehran has WtE project under development. Organic fraction high (~55%).

msw_biogenic_frac.source: MENA regional benchmarks; Iran LMIC organic-rich waste

msw_treatment.source: EcoMENA; biosaline.org doi:10.1177/0734242X211068236

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: FAO 2022 cattle ~9M + sheep ~50M + goats ~25M + poultry ~500M; standard excretion factors × 12% DM
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large sheep/goat herds, mostly extensive. Industrial poultry sector growing.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 87M pop × ~40% treatment × 25 g DS/person/day × 365 / 1e9

nutrient_status_source: FAO; arid/semi-arid soils generally low organic matter and nutrients
notes: GEOPOLITICAL RISK: US/EU sanctions severely restrict international investment. Frontier cannot currently operate here. Large theoretical resource noted for scenario planning. Sugarcane mills in Khuzestan represent best concentrated feedstock.

name: Iraq

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: FAOSTAT 2022 wheat ~4 Mt + barley ~1 Mt + rice ~0.4 Mt + dates ~0.7 Mt × RPR × 30% recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Wheat and barley straw dominant. Date palm fronds. Tigris-Euphrates agricultural zone concentrated.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: FAO FRA 2020; Iraq has negligible natural forest; date palm plantations
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Essentially no commercial forestry

msw_total_mt.source: JICA Iraq SWM study; calc: 42M pop × 0.52 kg/cap/day; Bagdad ~3 Mt/yr
msw_total_mt.notes: Primarily open dumping. Formal waste management collapsed in conflict areas. Baghdad improving.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: MENA regional benchmarks; Iraq LMIC-MIC transitional

msw_treatment.source: JICA Iraq SWM study (openjicareport.jica.go.jp)

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: FAO 2022 cattle ~2.8M + sheep ~6.5M + goats ~2M + poultry ~90M; standard excretion factors

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 42M pop × ~25% treatment × 25 g DS/person/day × 365 / 1e9

nutrient_status_source: FAO; arid soils, salinization widespread in Mesopotamian plains
notes: GOVERNANCE RISK: Post-conflict state, ongoing instability in parts of country, militia/corruption issues. Limited near-term BiCRS viability. Wheat/barley straw noted for long-term scenario only.

name: Kazakhstan

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: FAOSTAT 2022 wheat ~18 Mt × 1.3 RPR + barley ~3 Mt × 1.2 + sunflower ~2 Mt × 2.0 + cotton residues × 30% recoverable; IEA Bioenergy Task 40
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Kazakh steppe wheat belt (North Kazakhstan, Kostanay, Akmola) is world's largest contiguous dryland wheat zone. Enormous straw resource but very low population density and infrastructure — logistics highly challenging.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: FAO FRA 2020 Kazakhstan; small forest area (mostly saxaul/scrub); some plantation
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Negligible commercial forestry

msw_total_mt.source: Wikipedia KAZ waste; Astana Times 2019; calc: 19M pop × 0.65 kg/cap/day; 4.3 Mt cited for 2018
msw_total_mt.notes: Near-total open dumping (~97%). Some recycling (3–5%). No WtE.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: MDPI Energies 2024 KAZ MSW composition study: food waste ~45% + paper ~15% = ~60%; adjusted 0.58

msw_treatment.source: Wikipedia KAZ waste management; Astana Times 2019; MDPI su17198696

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: FAO 2022 cattle ~7.5M + sheep ~18M + horses ~3M + camels ~0.2M + poultry ~40M; standard excretion factors
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large pastoral herds; very low collectability outside industrial zones

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 19M pop × ~55% treatment (Almaty/Nur-Sultan well-served) × 25 g DS/person/day × 365 / 1e9

nutrient_status_source: FAO; steppe soils naturally low fertility; extensive dryland farming
notes: Enormous wheat straw resource but infrastructure extremely sparse. No CCS storage sites identified. Governance: moderate (authoritarian but functional state). Biomass burial (no storage needed) may be most viable pathway if governance/logistics improve. Very long-term scenario.

name: Israel

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: FAOSTAT 2022 wheat ~0.7 Mt + citrus ~1 Mt + vegetables + cotton + olive prunings × RPR × 30% recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very small total ag sector. Citrus and olive prunings. Cotton ginning waste. Modest resource.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: FAO FRA 2020; KKL-JNF planted forests small total area
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very small planted forest sector

msw_total_mt.source: World Bank WaW 2.0; OECD data; calc: 9.3M pop × 1.70 kg/cap/day (high-income rate)
msw_total_mt.notes: ~70% to landfill; ~24% recycling/composting; ~5% WtE (Hiriya plant). Israel has EU-comparable waste stats.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: OECD-comparable; Israel HIC composition; ~30% food + ~25% paper = ~55%; adjusted 0.52

msw_treatment.source: World Bank WaW 2.0; Israel EMA annual report

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: FAO 2022 cattle ~0.4M + poultry ~55M + pigs (limited); intensive livestock systems
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Very intensive confined livestock systems — high collectability relative to herd size

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 9.3M pop × ~90% treatment × 25 g DS/person/day × 365 / 1e9
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Among world's highest WWTP coverage and water reuse rates

nutrient_status_source: FAO; intensive agriculture with very high fertilizer use; Mediterranean coastal soils high-input
notes: Strong governance, high-tech. Small country, limited biomass resource but excellent institutional capacity. Hiriya WtE complex near Tel Aviv is potential BiCRS site. Geologic storage uncertain — Mediterranean offshore or Jordan Rift Valley options unclear. More relevant as technology hub than feedstock source.

name: United Arab Emirates

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: FAOSTAT 2022 dates ~0.9 Mt (fronds/pits) + vegetables + feed crops × RPR × 30% recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Date palm fronds only significant residue. Very limited agriculture in desert environment.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: FAO FRA 2020; UAE has negligible natural forest; mangrove plantings only
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Negligible

msw_total_mt.source: EcoMENA Middle East; calc: 10M pop × 1.78 kg/cap/day (very high-income, high waste rate); biosaline.org MENA study
msw_total_mt.notes: Dubai/Abu Dhabi WtE plants operational (Sharjah). ~35% WtE, ~50% landfill, ~15% recycling. Most advanced waste infrastructure in Middle East.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: EcoMENA; UAE HIC-MIC profile; ~25% food + ~22% paper = ~47%; rounded 0.48

msw_treatment.source: EcoMENA; Sharjah WtE plant data; Dubai Municipality waste reports

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: FAO 2022 camels ~0.1M + goats/sheep ~2M + poultry ~20M; standard excretion factors
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Small pastoral/zoo livestock. Concentrated poultry in Al Ain.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 10M pop × ~90% treatment × 25 g DS/person/day × 365 / 1e9
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Near-universal WWTP coverage

nutrient_status_source: FAO; desert soils; very low natural fertility
notes: Very limited biomass resource but strong state capacity, high investment appetite, and existing WtE (Sharjah). UAE is interested in CCS (ADNOC CCUS hubs). WtE + CCS on existing Sharjah/Dubai plants is most viable BiCRS pathway. Small scale nationally but high symbolic/political importance. UAE hosts COP28 — climate ambition high.

name: Alberta

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan crop production Nov 2023 (wheat 9.3 Mt, canola 5.4 Mt, barley 3.2 Mt, oats 0.7 Mt) × crop-specific RPR × 0.85 odt factor × removal cap (30% for cereals, 15% for canola). Wheat: 9.3×1.3×0.85×0.30=3.08 Mt; canola: 5.4×1.5×0.85×0.15=1.03 Mt; barley: 3.2×1.1×0.85×0.30=0.90 Mt; oats: 0.7×1.2×0.85×0.30=0.21 Mt. Total ~5.22 Mt.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Canola straw removal capped at 15% (lower than cereals) because: fine/brittle texture reduces collection efficiency; soil organic matter benefits favor incorporation; competing wind-erosion control value on Alberta dryland soils. Cereal straw at 30% (conservative vs 40%) per REAP-Canada Canadian crop residue supply review. Prairie biomass share AB≈35% consistent with literature (Mabee & Saddler 2010, Biomass Bioenergy). Consistent with national CAN record (19 Mt) when provinces summed.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: National Forestry Database (NRCan) 2022 total Canada logging residues ~21 Mt ODT/yr; Alberta share ~8–10% based on AAC ~22.5 million m3 (Alberta ENR, 2021) and residue factor 0.18 odt/m3 roundwood
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Alberta forest harvest concentrated in boreal north (Peace River, Slave Lake). AAC ~22.5 million m3 × residue factor ~0.18 odt/m3 = ~4.0 Mt gross logging residue; recoverable fraction ~45% given remote access and slash burning practices → ~1.8 Mt. Literature (Slade et al. 2014) puts AB at ~2 Mt ODT range.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: StatCan 2022 Waste Management Survey (dq240702b); Alberta population 4.26M (2021 Census) × ~880 kg/capita disposed (StatCan 2022 per-capita rate for AB, highest in Canada) + diversion ~200 kg/capita = ~1,080 kg/capita total generation
msw_total_mt.notes: Alberta has highest per-capita waste disposal in Canada at ~880 kg/capita (StatCan 2022). Total MSW generation including diversion ~4.1 Mt. Predominantly landfilled; minor WtE capacity.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: ECCC NPRI waste composition data; World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018) Canada analogue ~0.55–0.60 biogenic for high-income cold-climate provinces
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Lower organic fraction than national average due to relatively high plastic/construction waste share in Alberta's energy sector economy.

msw_treatment.source: StatCan Waste Management Survey 2022; ECCC Solid Waste Diversion and Disposal indicators; Canadian Infrastructure Council 2023

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan Livestock Estimates Jan 2023 (AB = 42.7% of 11.3M cattle = 4.83M head, plus ~400k hogs, ~130k dairy). Beef cattle: 4.5M head × 5.5 t wet/head/yr × 0.12 dry fraction = 2.97 Mt dry; dairy: 0.13M × 20 t wet × 0.12 = 0.31 Mt; feedlot cattle add concentrated manure. Total with poultry/hogs ~5.8 Mt dry.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Alberta is Canada's dominant beef province (feedlots concentrated in Lethbridge/Brooks). StatCan 2023: 4.83M cattle. Manure dry-matter factors: beef 0.10–0.14, dairy 0.10–0.12 (IEA Biogas Outlook 2020, Task 37). High uncertainty on dry fraction. Canada total livestock manure ~21 Mt dry (IEA/FAO).

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: Canada national biosolids 666,000 dry t/yr (CCME Canada-Wide Approach for Management of Wastewater Biosolids); Alberta share = 4.26M / 36.99M national pop = 11.5% → ~76,500 t/yr. CCME biosolids report; StatCan 2021 Census population.
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Population-scaled from national 666 kt/yr. Calgary and Edmonton WWTPs are primary sources.

nutrient_status_source: FAO FAOSTAT fertilizer use per ha 2022; AAFC Nutrient Management reports; Alberta cropland generally under fertilizer pressure relative to global excess zones
notes: Alberta is Canada's leading cattle province and a major grain (wheat, canola, barley) producer. Ag residues and manure dominate. Forestry residues meaningful but access-limited in boreal north. Highest per-capita MSW in Canada (resource economy). No WtE capacity as of 2023.

name: British Columbia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: BC crop production minimal; Peace River region produces small grains (~0.3 Mt wheat, ~0.1 Mt canola, ~0.1 Mt barley). RPR × 0.85 odt × removal cap (30% cereals, 15% canola): wheat 0.3×1.3×0.85×0.30=0.10 Mt; canola 0.1×1.5×0.85×0.15=0.02 Mt; barley 0.1×1.1×0.85×0.30=0.03 Mt. Hay residues not recoverable. Total ~0.18 Mt.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: BC has limited arable land (~2.5M ha, much in Peace River district near Alberta border). Hay and forage dominate total farmland; cereal/canola belt is primarily Peace River. StatCan 2023 crop report does not separately list BC for major grain crops. Agricultural residues are not a primary BiCRS feedstock for BC.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: NRCan Canadian Forest Service / Open Government Portal: Maps forecasting availability of logging residues in Canada (2021 dataset). BC = ~45–50% of national 21 Mt ODT/yr total. BC Hydro IRP biomass characterization (2015): 12 Mt dry/yr from existing industry. Search result: BC = 13.7 million BDT/yr (nearly half Canadian total).
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: BC is by far Canada's largest forestry province. Mountain pine beetle salvage harvest (2000s–2015) boosted residues; now declining as salvage wind-down. Coastal and Interior combined. Mill residues (sawdust, chips, bark) additional ~5 Mt but largely consumed in existing bioenergy. Logging slash and uneconomic residues estimated 7–14 Mt ODT/yr recoverable.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: BC population 5.0M (2021 Census) × ~573 kg/capita disposed (StatCan 2022: BC below-average disposal rate) + diversion ~250 kg/capita = ~820 kg/capita total → ~4.1 Mt; discounted slightly for high diversion rates. Fraser Institute 2018 data: BC 2.72 Mt disposed.
msw_total_mt.notes: BC has progressive waste diversion policy; Metro Vancouver has WtE facility. 2018 data shows 2.72 Mt disposed; with diversion and generation growth ~3.4 Mt total estimated for 2023.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: ECCC waste composition surveys; World Bank What a Waste 2.0 Canada analogue
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Relatively high organic/food waste fraction in BC urban areas.

msw_treatment.source: Metro Vancouver Integrated Solid Waste and Resource Management Plan; BC Ministry of Environment Recycling Regulation data 2022; ECCC Solid Waste indicators

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan Livestock Estimates 2023; BC cattle ~3% of national (0.34M head), dairy ~13% of national dairy herd (~160k cows, concentrated Fraser Valley). Poultry substantial. Cattle dry manure ~0.2 Mt; dairy ~0.38 Mt; poultry ~0.1 Mt → ~0.6 Mt dry total.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Fraser Valley is a concentrated livestock zone with nutrient management challenges. Dairy and poultry dominate over beef. Manure nutrient surplus in Lower Mainland.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: BC share of national 666 kt/yr biosolids (CCME). BC pop 5.0M / 37.0M = 13.5% → ~90 kt/yr. Genome BC notes ~38,000 dry t/yr for BC alone (older estimate, consistent with scale).
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Metro Vancouver SEFC and Annacis Island WWTPs are major sources. BC Biosolids Management Policy guides land application.

nutrient_status_source: BC Ministry of Agriculture Nutrient Management; Fraser Valley intensive livestock creates localized nutrient excess; broadly moderate province-wide
notes: BC is Canada's dominant forestry province. Logging residues are the principal BiCRS feedstock by far. Agricultural residues minor (limited arable land). Fraser Valley has concentrated dairy/poultry. Metro Vancouver WtE exists. Pine beetle salvage pulse now winding down reduces near-term forestry residue ceiling.

name: Manitoba

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan crop production Nov 2023 (wheat 5.1 Mt, canola 3.1 Mt, corn 1.8 Mt, soy 1.6 Mt, barley 1.2 Mt, oats 0.5 Mt). Wheat: 5.1×1.3×0.85×0.30=1.69 Mt; canola: 3.1×1.5×0.85×0.15=0.59 Mt; corn stover: 1.8×1.0×0.85×0.30=0.46 Mt; soy: 1.6×1.2×0.85×0.30=0.49 Mt; barley: 1.2×1.1×0.85×0.30=0.34 Mt; oats: 0.5×1.2×0.85×0.30=0.15 Mt. Total ~3.72 Mt.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Manitoba is 13% of Prairie grain belt. Also has significant corn stover (southern MB near US border). Canola straw capped at 15% removal. 2023 was drier-than-average on Prairies. Literature: Mabee et al. estimate MB at 5–7 Mt gross straw (before removal caps). Net available for bioenergy after livestock bedding competition ~2.5 Mt (low end).

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: MB roundwood harvest small (~4M m3/yr based on NRCan NFD proportional share); residue factor ~0.12 odt/m3 × 4M = 0.48 Mt; recoverable ~50% → ~0.25 Mt. Add mill residues. NRCan national total 21 Mt ODT; MB share <3%.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Manitoba boreal forest harvested mainly for pulpwood (Tolko). Harvest well below AAC. Forest residues secondary feedstock after ag.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: MB population 1.34M (2021 Census) × ~710 kg/capita total generation (StatCan 2022 national ~684 kg/capita disposal + ~200 kg diverted). Fraser Institute 2018: MB 0.963 Mt disposed.
msw_total_mt.notes: Winnipeg (~750k) dominates MSW. 2018 data 0.963 Mt is disposal only; total generation ~1.2 Mt including diversion; ~0.95 Mt conservative estimate for 2023.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 Canada analogue; ECCC composition data
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Typical Canadian mid-size province composition.

msw_treatment.source: City of Winnipeg Waste and Diversion reports; StatCan Waste Management Survey 2022

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan Livestock Estimates Jan 2023. MB hogs: ~13% of national 13.9M = 1.81M head × 1.8 t wet/yr × 0.08 dry = 0.26 Mt. MB cattle: ~6% of 11.3M = 0.68M × 5.5 t wet × 0.12 dry = 0.45 Mt. Dairy: ~8% national = 64k × 20 t wet × 0.12 = 0.15 Mt. Poultry ~0.1 Mt. Total wet basis ~17.5 Mt → dry ~1.8 Mt.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Manitoba has significant hog industry (Red River Valley). Cattle secondary. Hog manure production concentrated in Southern Manitoba.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: MB pop 1.34M / 37.0M = 3.6% of national 666 kt = ~24 kt/yr. Winnipeg 3 WWTPs produced ~12,800 dry t/yr in 2016 (City of Winnipeg Biosolids Master Plan) — consistent with provincial estimate.
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Winnipeg dominant WWTP source. Biosolids land-applied in southern Manitoba.

nutrient_status_source: AAFC Prairie nutrient management reports; MB ag nutrient balance generally moderate; CCME
notes: Manitoba sits at the transition between Prairies and boreal. Ag residues (cereal straw + corn stover) dominate. Hog industry produces concentrated manure in south. Forestry residues limited. No WtE as of 2023.

name: New Brunswick

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: NB agriculture small; StatCan 2021 Census of Agriculture. Principal crops: potatoes (1.2 Mt fresh weight, residues low-density), cereals small (<200 kt). Potato tops/vines: 1.2 Mt × 0.15 RPR × 0.40 = 0.07 Mt. Cereal straw from REAP-Canada: Atlantic provinces 185 kt straw; NB ~30% of Atlantic = 74 kt. Total ~0.15 Mt.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: NB agriculture dominated by potatoes (northwest and central). Potato tops/vines are wet and not easily recovered. Cereal straw minor. Total recoverable ag residues small.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: NB Forest Biomass to Energy Atlas (GNB 2012): total annual potential harvest 9.77 Mt GMT merchantable + 4.25 Mt GMT residual biomass + 1.50 Mt GMT bark; residual biomass = 4.25 Mt GMT × 0.45 dry fraction = 1.91 Mt ODT gross; recoverable ~45% = 0.86 Mt. NRCan NFD: NB roundwood harvest ~5–6 million m3/yr; residue factor ~0.15 odt/m3 recoverable.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: NB is heavily forested (5.9M ha commercial forest). J.D. Irving and other major operators. Mountain pine beetle not a factor; mixed softwood/hardwood. Forest biomass historically burned as slash or left on site; recovery improving.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: NB population 0.776M (2021 Census) × ~670 kg/capita total generation (StatCan 2022: NB 651 kg/capita disposed; + ~100 kg diverted). 0.776M × 0.670 t = 0.52 Mt.
msw_total_mt.notes: NB has moderate per-capita waste. Limited waste diversion infrastructure outside Moncton/Fredericton/Saint John.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 Canada analogue; ECCC

msw_treatment.source: StatCan Waste Management Survey 2022; NB Dept. of Environment & Local Government

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: NB livestock: StatCan 2023 estimates ~200k cattle, ~75k hogs, ~25k dairy cows, poultry significant (McCain country). Cattle: 0.2M × 5.5 t wet × 0.12 dry = 0.13 Mt; hogs: 0.075M × 1.8 t × 0.08 = 0.011 Mt; dairy: 0.025M × 20 t × 0.12 = 0.06 Mt; poultry: ~0.03 Mt. Total ~0.22 Mt.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: NB has modest livestock; some potato-associated hog operations in northwest.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: NB pop 0.776M / 37.0M = 2.1% × 666 kt = ~14 kt/yr (CCME national biosolids total).
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Population-scaled from CCME national total.

nutrient_status_source: AAFC; NB soil nutrient surveys; potato-intensive areas may have localized nutrient loading but province-wide low
notes: New Brunswick is predominantly forested. Forestry residues are the dominant biomass stream. Agriculture (potato-focused) contributes modestly. J.D. Irving is a major integrated forest company. Biomass already used in kraft pulp mill energy recovery.

name: Newfoundland and Labrador

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: NL agriculture extremely limited; StatCan 2021 Census of Agriculture: ~430k ha total farmland, mostly pasture. Turnip/root vegetable production minor. REAP-Canada Eastern Canada: Atlantic provinces <200 kt total cereal straw; NL <5%.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: NL has negligible arable agriculture. Small hay, vegetable, and root crop sector. Ag residues not a meaningful feedstock.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: NL has Boreal forest (Corner Brook Pulp and Paper). NRCan NFD roundwood harvest ~3–4 million m3/yr in NL; residue factor ~0.10–0.12 odt/m3 recoverable × 3.5M m3 = 0.35–0.42 Mt gross; recoverable ~50% given remote terrain = ~0.18–0.21 Mt; add mill residues ~0.15 Mt → total ~0.35 Mt.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Corner Brook Pulp and Paper is major forest industry anchor. Labrador forestry limited. Remote terrain constrains residue recovery.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: NL population 0.511M (2021 Census) × ~700 kg/capita total generation. StatCan 2022 disposal data (decline of 1,741 t residential waste from 2020 to 2022 noted). ~0.35 Mt estimated total generation.
msw_total_mt.notes: St. John's metro dominates MSW generation.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 Canada analogue

msw_treatment.source: StatCan Waste Management Survey 2022; Multi-Materials Stewardship Board NL

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: NL livestock very limited; StatCan 2023 — NL has ~15k cattle, ~25k hogs, ~10k dairy. Dry manure total ~0.04 Mt. Population-scaled from national 21 Mt dry: NL ~0.2% of livestock → ~0.04 Mt.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Livestock sector very small. NL is not a significant agricultural province.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: NL pop 0.511M / 37.0M = 1.38% × 666 kt = ~9.2 kt/yr (CCME national biosolids figure).
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: St. John's Harbour WWTP major source.

nutrient_status_source: AAFC; minimal agricultural nutrient pressure in NL
notes: NL is sparsely populated with limited agriculture. Forestry residues are the primary biomass feedstock, though harvest levels are modest. Corner Brook Pulp and Paper uses mill residues internally. Remote communities have high per-capita MSW disposal.

name: Northwest Territories

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: NWT has negligible commercial agriculture. StatCan 2021 Census of Agriculture: <500 ha farmland. No commercial crop residues.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Territory. No commercial agriculture. Near-zero ag residues. Do not use for BiCRS planning.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: NWT has boreal forest but negligible commercial forestry harvest (<0.1 million m3/yr). NRCan NFD data. Harvest dominated by small-scale and indigenous community use.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Mostly intact boreal. Limited commercial logging. Negligible harvest residues at scale relevant for BiCRS.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: NWT population 41,070 (2021 Census) × ~850 kg/capita (remote territory; higher per-capita generation due to packaging, import goods, limited recycling) = ~0.035 Mt.
msw_total_mt.notes: Remote communities; virtually all waste landfilled or open-burned. StatCan does not publish NWT separately in main waste tables.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: Estimated; remote northern communities have higher packaging/non-biogenic fraction

msw_treatment.source: GNWT Environmental Protection Division; ECCC Northern Waste Management

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: negligible livestock; wild game not counted in manure feedstock; StatCan 2021 Census of Agriculture NWT.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Near-zero. No commercial livestock operations.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: NWT pop 41,070 / 37.0M = 0.11% × 666 kt national = ~0.74 kt/yr. Most communities use lagoon treatment rather than conventional WWTP with sludge.
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Many remote NWT communities use sewage lagoons with no sludge suitable for BiCRS.

nutrient_status_source: No commercial agriculture; no nutrient pressure
notes: Territory with negligible biomass feedstocks at BiCRS-relevant scale. All values near-zero. Population centres (Yellowknife) produce modest MSW. Do not include in national biomass supply totals for planning purposes. Values provided for map completeness only.

name: Nova Scotia

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: NS agriculture: apples, blueberries, hay, small cereals. REAP-Canada Eastern Canada: Atlantic provinces 185 kt cereal straw; NS ~35% of Atlantic = 65 kt. Add blueberry/orchard prunings ~15 kt. Hay residues not recoverable. Total ~0.10 Mt.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Nova Scotia has modest diverse agriculture; no major grain crops. Wild blueberry prunings represent niche feedstock. Ag residues are not a primary BiCRS feedstock.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: NS total forest harvest 2018 = 3.36 million m3 roundwood (NS Dept Natural Resources stats); residue factor ~0.13 odt/m3 recoverable; 3.36M × 0.13 = 0.44 Mt gross; recoverable ~100% (most accessible terrain) → ~0.44 Mt. Add unmerchantable biomass. Cross-check: Nova Scotia Feedstock Supply 2021 report cited in search results.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: NS forests 68% privately owned. Significant softwood (spruce-fir) used for pulp. Historical harvest to Northern Pulp; closure 2020 reduced harvest. Biomass residues from remaining operations + hardwood stand thinnings.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: NS population 0.969M (2021 Census) × ~540 kg/capita total generation (StatCan 2022: NS lowest disposal at 386 kg/capita + diversion ~150 kg = ~536 kg/capita total). 0.969M × 0.54 t = 0.52 Mt.
msw_total_mt.notes: Nova Scotia has best waste diversion rate in Canada (43% in 2022; up from 33% in 2002). Per-capita disposal among lowest nationally. Cape Breton and HRM are primary generators.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: ECCC; NS organic waste program diverts significant food waste separately; residual has moderate biogenic fraction
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: NS has mandatory organics diversion; residual MSW biogenic fraction somewhat lower than provinces without organics diversion.

msw_treatment.source: ECCC Solid Waste Diversion and Disposal indicators 2022; Resource Recovery Fund Board NS

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: NS livestock: ~85k cattle, ~30k hogs, ~30k dairy, significant poultry (Maple Leaf). Cattle dry: 0.085M × 5.5 t wet × 0.12 = 0.056 Mt; dairy: 0.030M × 20 t × 0.12 = 0.072 Mt; hogs + poultry ~0.04 Mt. Total ~0.17 Mt wet basis → dry ~0.12 Mt.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Annapolis Valley agriculture has some intensive livestock. Dairy concentrated in Colchester/Pictou counties.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: NS pop 0.969M / 37.0M = 2.62% × 666 kt = ~17.5 kt/yr (CCME national biosolids).
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Halifax Water (HRM) is primary WWTP source; biosolids land-applied or composted.

nutrient_status_source: AAFC; NS soils nutrient-poor; organic production important
notes: Nova Scotia is a small, heavily forested province with strong waste diversion but limited biomass at scale. Forestry residues are primary feedstock. Northern Pulp mill closure (2020) reduced demand for wood fibre, increasing potential residues. Province-wide biomass potential modest in absolute terms.

name: Nunavut

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: No commercial agriculture in Nunavut. StatCan 2021 Census of Agriculture: 0 commercial farms.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Territory. Arctic climate. No agriculture. Value is definitionally zero.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: No commercial forestry in Nunavut. Treeline is below Nunavut. NRCan National Forestry Database.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Territory. Above treeline. No forest biomass resource at BiCRS-relevant scale.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: Nunavut population 36,858 (2021 Census) × ~800 kg/capita (remote Arctic communities; high packaging import, no recycling). StatCan does not report Nunavut separately.
msw_total_mt.notes: 25 remote communities; virtually all waste open-dumped or landfilled. Major logistics cost for any waste treatment. MSW not a practical BiCRS feedstock given scale and remoteness.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: Estimated; high packaging fraction in Arctic community waste streams
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Remote community waste is relatively high in non-biogenic packaging materials.

msw_treatment.source: Government of Nunavut Solid Waste Management Strategy; ECCC Northern Waste Management reports

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: No commercial livestock in Nunavut. StatCan 2021 Census of Agriculture.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Near-zero. Some sled dogs and subsistence animals not counted.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: Nunavut pop 36,858 / 37.0M = 0.10% × 666 kt = ~0.66 kt/yr. Most communities use trucked-haul or lagoon sewage; no conventional WWTP sludge.
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Lagoon treatment dominant; no recoverable sludge in conventional sense.

nutrient_status_source: No agriculture; Arctic substrate; no nutrient pressure
notes: Territory. No meaningful biomass feedstocks. All values near-zero. Included for map completeness only. Arctic communities face energy security challenges but BiCRS is not applicable at territorial scale.

name: Ontario

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan crop production Nov 2023 (corn 9.6 Mt, soy 4.0 Mt, wheat 1.5 Mt, barley 0.2 Mt, oats 0.1 Mt). Corn stover: 9.6×1.0×0.85×0.30=2.45 Mt; soy: 4.0×1.2×0.85×0.30=1.22 Mt; wheat: 1.5×1.3×0.85×0.30=0.50 Mt; barley: 0.2×1.1×0.85×0.30=0.056 Mt; oats: 0.1×1.2×0.85×0.30=0.031 Mt. Total ~4.26 Mt. Cross-check: REAP-Canada Ontario corn stover 1,900 kt + cereal 615 kt available (lower bound after feed/bedding competition).
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Ontario is Canada's largest corn and soybean province. Corn stover is the dominant residue. REAP-Canada lower bound ~2.5 Mt net available after livestock competition. Literature: Ontario corn stover 3.8 Mt ODT/yr gross (from search results — consistent). 30% removal cap for corn stover balances soil carbon requirements in Ontario clay soils.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: Ontario roundwood harvest ~13-15 million m3/yr (NRCan NFD proportional share of 129.5 M m3 national; ON historically ~10%); residue factor ~0.15 odt/m3 harvested = 1.95–2.25 Mt gross; recoverable ~50–60% given mixed Crown/private land access = ~1.0–1.35 Mt. Add mill residues from sawmills/pulpmills ~1.0–1.5 Mt. Total ~2.5 Mt. Cross-check: Ontario ~12% of national 21 Mt ODT = 2.5 Mt aligns.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Ontario boreal and Great Lakes-St. Lawrence mixed forests. Harvest concentrated in Northern Ontario (Timmins, Kapuskasing corridor). Some surplus forest growth given reduced industry (post-2008). Southern Ontario has minimal commercial forestry.

msw_total_mt.source: StatCan Waste Management Survey 2022; Fraser Institute: Ontario 10.09 Mt disposed in 2018; per capita 925.5 kg/person in 2022 (highest growth). Ontario pop 14.22M × ~800 kg/capita total generation = 11.4 Mt. StatCan 2022 report notes Ontario per-capita disposal rose 5% to 925 kg disposal-only.
msw_total_mt.notes: Ontario is by far Canada's largest MSW generator. GTA alone exports ~3.5 Mt to Michigan landfills. Durham, Peel, Simcoe have WtE or planned WtE. 2018 Fraser Institute disposal data 10.09 Mt, updated for population and trend growth to ~11.5 Mt total generation 2023.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: ECCC NPRI; Ontario MOE waste audits; World Bank What a Waste 2.0 Canada
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Ontario residential waste has ~58% biogenic (food, paper, wood). Commercial/industrial slightly lower.

msw_treatment.source: Ontario MOE Waste-Free Ontario strategy; Veolia/Canadian Infrastructure Council 2023; Durham WtE facility; Peel Region WtE approved

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan Livestock Estimates Jan 2023. ON cattle: 14% of 11.3M = 1.58M head × 5.5 t wet × 0.12 dry = 1.04 Mt; dairy: ON has ~30% of national dairy herd ~285k cows × 20 t wet × 0.12 = 0.68 Mt; hogs: ~25% of 13.9M = 3.5M × 1.8 t wet × 0.08 = 0.50 Mt; poultry significant (~30% national) → ~0.4 Mt dry. Total ~2.62 Mt, rounded to 2.8 Mt.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Ontario has major dairy (southwestern ON), hog (Perth/Oxford counties), and poultry industries. Concentrated livestock operations create nutrient management issues. Manure biogas (anaerobic digestion) already significant in Ontario under FIT/microFIT programs.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: Ontario Biosolids Council: ~217,000 dry t/yr representing ~60% of Ontario municipal biosolids → total ~362 kt/yr (from search results, 217 kt = 60% of ON total). Cross-check: ON pop 14.22M / 37.0M = 38.4% × 666 kt national = 256 kt/yr — consistent.
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Toronto WWTP (Ashbridges Bay, Highland Creek, Humber) are among largest in Canada. Biosolids land-applied and heat-dried for agricultural use. Ontario Ontario Biosolids Council figure cited.

nutrient_status_source: AAFC Nutrient management in Ontario; intensive livestock sectors (hog, dairy, poultry) in SW Ontario create localized nutrient surpluses (Oxford, Perth, Huron, Wellington counties); province-wide moderate
notes: Ontario is Canada's most populous province and a major agricultural producer. Corn stover and soy residues dominate ag feedstocks. Large WWTP biosolids stream. Significant MSW with growing WtE interest. Forest residues meaningful in northern Ontario. Concentrated livestock operations in SW Ontario already target AD/biogas.

name: Prince Edward Island

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: PEI agriculture: potatoes (~1.2 Mt fresh), cereals (~200 kt), soybeans minor, hay. Potato tops/vines: 1.2 Mt × 0.08 dry RPR × 0.40 = 0.038 Mt; cereal straw: REAP-Canada Atlantic provinces 185 kt; PEI ~30% of Atlantic = 55 kt = 0.055 Mt; crop residues total ~0.10 Mt. With soybean/canola minor additions ~0.12 Mt.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: PEI is the most intensively farmed province by land area share. Potatoes dominate. Potato tops and vines wet and logistically difficult. Cereal (wheat, barley, oats) straw more recoverable. Small province — absolute numbers low.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: PEI forest harvest minimal (~0.5 million m3/yr); residue factor ~0.10 odt/m3; 0.5M × 0.10 = 0.05 Mt. Forests are 91% private woodlots (scattered, low harvest rates).
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: PEI is 91% private forest — scattered woodlots. Very limited commercial forestry. Forest residues essentially negligible for BiCRS.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: PEI population 154,331 (2021 Census) × ~650 kg/capita total generation = 0.10 Mt. StatCan: PEI excluded from main waste tables due to data gaps.
msw_total_mt.notes: Charlottetown WtE facility (Charlottetown Area Municipalities) is one of few small Canadian WtE operations. ~55,000 t/yr processed at WtE.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 Canada analogue; PEI waste characterization studies

msw_treatment.source: Charlottetown Area Municipalities WtE Facility (55,000 t/yr); PEI Dept. of Environment Energy & Forestry; search result: Charlottetown listed as WtE operator

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: PEI is intensively farmed; StatCan livestock — small cluster of hogs and dairy despite small land area. PEI ~5% of Atlantic hog production, ~8k dairy cows, ~50k cattle. StatCan 2006 manure profile: PEI listed as small cluster. Estimate: cattle 50k × 5.5 × 0.12 = 0.033 Mt; dairy 8k × 20 × 0.12 = 0.019 Mt; hogs 30k × 1.8 × 0.08 = 0.004 Mt; poultry significant for land area ~0.04 Mt. Total ~0.10 Mt.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: PEI has intensive potato-hog rotations creating nutrient pressure (manure used as potato fertilizer). Chicken Farmers of PEI significant. Manure nutrient loading is a local environmental issue.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: PEI pop 154,331 / 37.0M = 0.42% × 666 kt = ~2.8 kt/yr (CCME national total).
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Charlottetown WWTP primary source.

nutrient_status_source: PEI Dept. Agriculture: intensive potato-livestock rotation creates localized phosphorus loading in runoff; province-wide elevated compared to other Atlantic provinces
notes: PEI is small but intensively farmed. Potato/cereal rotation dominates. WtE in Charlottetown serves a higher % of waste than any other province. Nutrient management (potato-manure cycling) is a key local issue that intersects with biochar/BiCRS pathways. Absolute biomass quantities small.

name: Quebec

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan crop production Nov 2023 (corn 3.3 Mt, soy 1.3 Mt, wheat 0.5 Mt, oats 0.3 Mt). Corn stover: 3.3×1.0×0.85×0.30=0.84 Mt; soy: 1.3×1.2×0.85×0.30=0.40 Mt; wheat: 0.5×1.3×0.85×0.30=0.17 Mt; oats: 0.3×1.2×0.85×0.30=0.092 Mt. Total ~1.50 Mt. Cross-check: REAP-Canada Quebec corn stover 1,115 kt + cereal 880 kt available = 2.0 Mt (at higher removal rate) — consistent as upper bound.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Quebec literature gives 5.88 Mt dry total crop residue production (gross, before any removal caps). At 30% removal: ~1.5 Mt recoverable. REAP-Canada's 2.0 Mt figure for QC uses ~40% removal rate and is taken as upper bound. Corn and soy concentrated in Montérégie and Lanaudière regions (St. Lawrence lowlands).

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: National 21 Mt ODT total; QC = second largest forest province, ~25% of national = ~5.25 Mt ODT. Cross-check: Green hydrogen study (Karayel 2025): QC forest residues rank 2nd with 273.89 kt H2 potential, implying ~9 Mt ODT feedstock; BC 373 kt → ~12 Mt. QC/BC ratio ~75%, consistent with 5.5 Mt relative to BC ~10 Mt.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Quebec boreal forest (La Tuque, Abitibi, Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean regions) is heavily harvested for softwood pulp/lumber. Major forest companies: Resolute, Domtar, Uniboard. Forest sector residues already used heavily in kraft mill energy; 'accessible' residues are surplus beyond industrial consumption.

msw_total_mt.source: Fraser Institute: QC 5.56 Mt disposed in 2018; StatCan 2022: QC highest per-capita residential disposal (378 kg/capita residential); pop 8.5M × ~660 kg/capita total generation = 5.6 Mt. Growth trend modest.
msw_total_mt.notes: Quebec is second-largest MSW generator. Quebec City WtE (Tricentris, Enviro Connexions) and Montreal-area WtE projects. Province has deposit-refund system reducing certain waste streams.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: ECCC waste composition; QC MDDEFP waste characterization studies; World Bank What a Waste 2.0

msw_treatment.source: Recyc-Québec annual waste management data 2022; ECCC Solid Waste indicators; Quebec City WtE facility operational

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan Livestock Estimates Jan 2023. QC hogs: ~32% of national 13.9M = 4.45M × 1.8 t wet × 0.08 dry = 0.64 Mt; QC dairy: ~37% of national herd ~350k cows × 20 t wet × 0.12 dry = 0.84 Mt; QC cattle: ~8% of 11.3M = 0.90M × 5.5 t wet × 0.12 = 0.59 Mt; poultry significant ~0.4 Mt. Manure cluster in St. Lawrence lowlands. Total ~2.47 Mt dry; adding poultry and smaller livestock = ~3.2 Mt.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Quebec is Canada's largest hog and dairy province by combined intensity. Montérégie region is a concentrated livestock zone. Manure biogas (AD) already deployed (Bioénergie La Tuque, Enerkem adjacent infrastructure). StatCan 2006 profile: QC is one of three major manure clusters.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: QC pop 8.5M / 37.0M = 23.0% × 666 kt national = ~153 kt/yr (CCME). Montreal WWTP (largest in Canada by flow) alone produces significant biosolids.
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Montreal WWTP is largest in Canada. Biosolids land-applied or composted; some incinerated. Quebec has structured biosolids management framework.

nutrient_status_source: MELCCFP QC: Montérégie and Chaudière-Appalaches regions have phosphorus surplus from concentrated hog/dairy operations; province-wide moderate elevated; AAFC agri-environmental indicators
notes: Quebec has large forestry and agriculture sectors. Forestry residues dominate by volume (boreal logging), but hog/dairy manure biogas is a significant co-feedstock. Strong policy environment (carbon market, RNG mandates). Montreal WWTP biosolids are a high-quality concentrated feedstock. Corn belt in southern QC is Canada's second-largest corn zone.

name: Saskatchewan

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan crop production Nov 2023 (wheat 14.2 Mt, canola 9.7 Mt, barley 4.6 Mt, oats 1.3 Mt). Wheat: 14.2×1.3×0.85×0.30=4.71 Mt; canola: 9.7×1.5×0.85×0.15=1.86 Mt; barley: 4.6×1.1×0.85×0.30=1.29 Mt; oats: 1.3×1.2×0.85×0.30=0.40 Mt. Total ~8.26 Mt. Literature cross-check: SK wheat straw alone 5.8 Mt ODT (REAP-Canada); SK accessible biomass 7.9 Mt (Prairie GIS study). REAP-Canada: SK = 52% of Prairie total 56.3 Mt gross × 0.52 = 29.3 Mt gross; at 30% cereal + 15% canola = ~8 Mt — consistent.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Saskatchewan is Canada's largest crop province and dominant ag-residue BiCRS province. Wheat straw is most logistically accessible. Canola straw capped at 15% removal due to fine/brittle texture, low bulk density, rapid decomposition, and soil C/wind-erosion retention value on Prairie soils. Literature consensus: 7.9–14 Mt recoverable depending on removal rate assumption. This estimate (8.2 Mt) is consistent with REAP-Canada and national record scaling.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: SK has limited commercial forestry; NRCan NFD: SK roundwood harvest ~3–5 million m3/yr (boreal north: Meadow Lake Tribal Council mills, Weyerhaeuser). Residue factor ~0.10 odt/m3 × 4M m3 = 0.40 Mt gross; recoverable ~50% = ~0.20 Mt. Add mill residues ~0.15 Mt. Also literature: Alberta and Saskatchewan residue yield ~24 and 15 ODT/ha respectively, but harvest area very limited in SK.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Saskatchewan forest industry is small relative to ag sector. Boreal forests in north-central SK (La Ronge area). Mill residues consumed internally. Limited harvesting intensity.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: SK population 1.133M (2021 Census) × ~880 kg/capita (StatCan 2022: SK among high-disposal provinces at ≥700 kg/capita disposal + diversion ~150 kg). 1.133M × 0.88 t = 1.0 Mt.
msw_total_mt.notes: Saskatchewan has high per-capita waste disposal (similar to Alberta, resource economy). Regina and Saskatoon dominate. Limited WtE capacity.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 Canada analogue; ECCC

msw_treatment.source: StatCan Waste Management Survey 2022; ECCC Saskatchewan waste data; SK Waste Reduction and Recycling Support program

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: StatCan Livestock Estimates Jan 2023. SK cattle: 19.3% of 11.3M = 2.18M head × 5.5 t wet × 0.12 dry = 1.44 Mt; SK hogs: ~8% of 13.9M = 1.11M × 1.8 × 0.08 = 0.16 Mt; dairy minor ~25k × 20 × 0.12 = 0.06 Mt; poultry ~0.05 Mt. Total ~1.71 Mt dry; rounded to 1.5 Mt central (some livestock on range, manure not recoverable).
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Saskatchewan cattle are primarily range/pasture beef (manure deposited on fields, lower recovery fraction than feedlot). Feedlot operations near Moose Jaw and Swift Current have concentrated manure. Recovery rate ~50% of calculated total.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: SK pop 1.133M / 37.0M = 3.06% × 666 kt = ~20.4 kt/yr (CCME national biosolids).
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Saskatoon and Regina WWTPs are primary sources.

nutrient_status_source: AAFC; SK soils have good nutrient capacity; not over-fertilized; organic matter conservation important for dryland agriculture
notes: Saskatchewan is Canada's largest grain province and the dominant BiCRS ag-residue province. Wheat straw and canola straw are primary feedstocks. Diffuse landscape (flatlands) favors mobile pyrolysis/biochar or bio-oil pathways. Forestry and MSW are secondary. Manure recovery challenging as most cattle are pasture-based.

name: Yukon

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: StatCan 2021 Census of Agriculture: Yukon has <100 commercial farms, primarily small-scale vegetable and forage. No commercial crop residues at BiCRS-relevant scale.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Territory. Sub-arctic climate. Negligible agriculture. Value effectively zero.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: Yukon has boreal/taiga forest but minimal commercial harvest (<0.2 million m3/yr). Spruce forests harvested for local lumber. NRCan NFD: Yukon commercial harvest very limited.
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Whitehorse-area small sawmills. Limited harvest. Forest residues not significant at territorial scale.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: Yukon population 40,232 (2021 Census) × ~850 kg/capita (remote territory premium; Whitehorse landfill serves entire territory). StatCan excludes territories from main waste tables.
msw_total_mt.notes: Whitehorse Yukon Solid Waste Facility serves most of territory.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: Estimated; remote territory waste composition

msw_treatment.source: Yukon Dept. of Community Services Solid Waste Management Strategy; ECCC Northern Waste

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: StatCan 2021 Census of Agriculture: negligible livestock in Yukon. No commercial operations.
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Near-zero. Some horses (tourism, recreation) not counted at scale.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: Yukon pop 40,232 / 37.0M = 0.11% × 666 kt = ~0.73 kt/yr (CCME). Whitehorse WWTP primary source.
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Whitehorse WWTP has land-application biosolids program.

nutrient_status_source: No meaningful agriculture; no nutrient pressure
notes: Territory. All biomass feedstocks near-zero at BiCRS-relevant scale. Included for map completeness only. Whitehorse is a small but complete city; local WtE or biochar from MSW could have community energy security value but not material for national BiCRS accounting.

name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: island UT, ~380 km² cultivated area (Agriculture Census 2015-16), minor coconut/paddy residue × RPR; 30% recoverable fraction
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Largely subsistence agriculture; coconut husk dominant residue

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ~86% forest cover (ISFR 2021, 6,743 km²); minimal logging activity; FAO residue factor ~0.5 t/ha/yr harvest residue on very low extraction rate
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Protected forest — very low commercial extraction; residue largely inaccessible

msw_total_mt.source: calc: population ~0.42 million (Census 2011 projected) × 380 g/capita/day (island town rate, CPCB 2020-21 national context); ×365
msw_total_mt.notes: Port Blair dominates; no state-specific CPCB figure — UT-level estimate

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018) lower-middle-income South Asia default; organic-rich tropical diet
msw_biogenic_frac.notes: Tropical island diet high in organic fraction

msw_treatment.source: CPCB Annual Report on SWM 2020-21; island UTs have limited treatment infrastructure

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: 20th Livestock Census 2019 A&N very small herd; ~15,000 cattle+buffalo × 12 kg/head/day dung × 0.20 DM fraction × 365 ÷ 1e6
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Tiny livestock population

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 0.42M pop × 50 L sewage/day × 50 mg TSS/L × 0.7 volatile solids × 365 ÷ 1e9; CPCB STP status: no operational STP reported for A&N (CPCB STP database 2021)
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: No operational STP; essentially zero formal sludge recovery

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer statistics; island subsistence agriculture, minimal synthetic fertilizer use
notes: Remote island UT; very small feedstock base. Forest cover is protected. BiCRS opportunity minimal.

name: Andhra Pradesh

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Hiloidhari et al. 2014 (Renew. Sustain. Energy Rev. 32:504-512) state-wise surplus residue; NPMCR 2014 gross residue data; ~30% recoverable applied to gross ~45 Mt
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Major crops: rice, sugarcane, maize, cotton, groundnut, pulses. State bifurcated from undivided AP in 2014 — these figures for post-bifurcation AP (coastal+Rayalaseema). Surplus residue range 13–24 Mt odt/yr after 40% recovery cap.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 forest area ~23,000 km² (17% of state); low logging rate; FAO-style residue factor 0.3 t/ha accessible residue
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Moderate forest cover in Eastern Ghats; low industrial forestry

msw_total_mt.source: calc: population ~53M (2021 est.) × 0.27 kg/capita/day (PMC9202976 Table 4, ~4,000 TPD for major AP cities scaled to state) × 365 ÷ 1e6; cross-checked CPCB 2020-21 state figure ~14,000 TPD AP+TG combined
msw_total_mt.notes: Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Tirupati are major generators

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018) India average; lower-middle-income South Asia ~55-60%

msw_treatment.source: CPCB Annual Report SWM 2020-21; AP reported 100% collection, partial treatment

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: Frontiers in Agronomy 2025 (doi:10.3389/fagro.2025.1689121) Table: AP total animal waste 29.1 Mt wet wt; × 0.20 dry-matter fraction
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large cattle and buffalo population; ~29 Mt wet dung → ~5.8 Mt odt

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~53M pop × 60% urban served by STP × 50 L/day × 40 mg VSS/L × 365 ÷ 1e9; CPCB STP database 2021 AP installed capacity ~1,200 MLD
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Partial STP coverage; significant untreated sewage

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer use per ha; AP ~130 kg/ha NPK (FAOSTAT/Deptt of Agriculture 2019-20)
notes: Good BiCRS potential from rice straw and sugarcane tops/bagasse. Large animal herd adds manure feedstock.

name: Arunachal Pradesh

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: small cultivated area ~0.3 Mha (Agriculture Census 2015-16); rice dominant crop; RPR 1.3, 30% recoverable; low productivity hillside farming
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Shifting cultivation (jhum); very sparse cropland in forested hill state

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 highest forest cover state — 79,917 km² forest; ~10% accessible with logging activity; residue factor 0.3 t/ha on accessible area; agroforestry residue additional
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Largest forest carbon stock in India (ISFR 2021). Low formal logging but significant agroforestry and firewood collection. Accessibility major constraint.

msw_total_mt.source: PMC9202976 Table 4: ~180 TPD for Arunachal Pradesh (2015 data); scaled to 2020 × 1.2 population growth factor × 365 ÷ 1e6
msw_total_mt.notes: Itanagar primary urban center

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); high organic fraction in NE India tribal/rural diet

msw_treatment.source: CPCB STP database 2021 — no STP reported for Arunachal Pradesh; minimal MSW infrastructure

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: 20th Livestock Census 2019 Arunachal ~500,000 cattle+mithun+pig; 12 kg/head/day × 0.20 DM × 365 ÷ 1e6
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Mithun (gayal) significant; free-ranging livestock

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~1.5M pop × very low STP coverage; CPCB: no operational STP in Arunachal Pradesh (2021)
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: No functional STP

nutrient_status_source: FAO/state agriculture dept; very low fertilizer use in jhum cultivation system
notes: Logistics and terrain severely limit feedstock accessibility. Forest residue is the dominant potential but not practically harvestable at scale.

name: Assam

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Hiloidhari et al. 2014; NPMCR: Assam ~2.65 Mt gross residue burned; total gross ~8-9 Mt; 30% recoverable applied; major crops: rice (3 seasons), jute, tea
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Rice dominant (Sali, Ahu, Boro seasons). Tea plantation pruning residue additional. Jute stick residue.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Assam forest area ~28,000 km²; moderate accessibility in Brahmaputra valley; residue factor 0.3 t/ha on ~30% accessible fraction
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Significant bamboo resources (also Bamboo Mission area) — relevant for biochar

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~35M pop × 0.35 kg/capita/day (NE India rate, PMC9202976) × 365 ÷ 1e6; Guwahati ~800 TPD (CPCB 2020-21)
msw_total_mt.notes: Guwahati dominant urban center; many small towns

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); NE India high organic fraction

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM Annual Report 2020-21

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: Frontiers in Agronomy 2025 (doi:10.3389/fagro.2025.1689121): Assam total animal waste 24.7 Mt wet wt; × 0.20 DM fraction
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Large cattle population in Brahmaputra floodplains; ~24.7 Mt wet → ~4.9 Mt odt

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~35M pop × 25% urban × 40% STP coverage × sewage rate; CPCB STP 2021: Assam limited STP capacity ~100 MLD
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Very low STP coverage

nutrient_status_source: FAO/state agriculture; ~70 kg/ha NPK, below national average; acidic soils with natural fertility constraints
notes: Flood-prone landscape complicates logistics. Bamboo residue underutilized BiCRS feedstock.

name: Bihar

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: NPMCR 2014 gross residue ~5.21 Mt for burning fraction; Hiloidhari et al. 2014 state-level; gross ~24 Mt (rice+wheat+maize); 30% recoverable = ~9.5 Mt odt surplus
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Major crops: rice, wheat, maize, sugarcane. Dense smallholder agriculture. Note: NPMCR figure of 5.21 Mt refers to burned fraction only, not total surplus.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Bihar forest cover ~7,300 km² (6.5% of state); very limited commercial forestry; residue factor 0.2 t/ha on small accessible area
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: One of least forested large states

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~128M pop (Census 2011 projected) × 0.27 kg/capita/day × 365 ÷ 1e6; low urbanization (~11%) reduces effective MSW; Patna ~1,500 TPD
msw_total_mt.notes: Low urbanization state but large population; significant rural organic waste

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); high organic fraction typical of low-income Indian states

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM Annual Report 2020-21; Bihar has limited waste treatment infrastructure

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: Frontiers in Agronomy 2025 (doi:10.3389/fagro.2025.1689121): Bihar total animal waste 48.1 Mt wet wt; × 0.20 DM fraction
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: ~48.1 Mt wet dung → ~9.6 Mt odt. Large cattle+buffalo herd supporting dairy economy.

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~128M pop × 11% urban × limited STP coverage; CPCB STP 2021: Bihar installed capacity ~250 MLD, mostly Patna
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Among lowest STP coverage in India

nutrient_status_source: Fertilizer consumption per hectare data 2019-20: Bihar 245 kg/ha (highest in India, Dept of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 2020); intensive rice-wheat belt
notes: Bihar has highest fertilizer use per ha nationally (245 kg/ha 2019-20) — nutrient-excess designation. Large rice-wheat residue potential but diffuse smallholder landscape.

name: Chandigarh

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: UT with <20 km² agricultural land; negligible crop production (Agriculture Census 2015-16)
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Entirely urban UT; near-zero ag residue

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: Sukhna Wildlife Sanctuary + urban green areas; minimal woody biomass residue
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Urban forest/parks only

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~1.18M pop × 0.82 kg/capita/day (high urban rate, CPCB 2020-21 Chandigarh ~950 TPD); Chandigarh SoE Report 2021 cites 950-1000 TPD
msw_total_mt.notes: Highly urbanized planned city; high per-capita waste generation

msw_biogenic_frac.source: Chandigarh SoE Report 2021; urban composition survey — lower organic fraction than national average due to higher income

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM Annual Report 2020-21; Chandigarh has WtE plant and relatively advanced MSW management

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: 20th Livestock Census 2019 minimal urban livestock; ~10,000 cattle equivalent
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Urban UT; negligible livestock

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 1.18M pop × ~85% STP coverage × 110 L/day × 40 mg VSS/L × 365 ÷ 1e9; well-served city
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Good STP infrastructure for India

nutrient_status_source: Urban UT — fertilizer use mainly horticultural; not classified as agricultural excess
notes: Entirely urban UT. MSW is dominant feedstock. Small but high-quality waste stream with existing WtE.

name: Chhattisgarh

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ~5.0 Mha net sown area (Agriculture Census 2015-16); dominant crop rice; RPR 1.3 × 7.5 Mt production × 30% recoverable ~4 Mt rice straw odt + minor wheat/maize; total ~5.5 Mt
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: 'Rice bowl of central India'; primarily single-crop (Kharif rice). Significant tribal smallholder agriculture.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Chhattisgarh forest area 55,611 km² (41% of state); moderate SAL/teak timber extraction; residue factor 0.3 t/ha on ~15% accessible fraction (8,300 km²)
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Third-largest forest state by area. Significant bamboo. Some industrial timber/paper mills.

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~32M pop × 0.27 kg/capita/day × 365 ÷ 1e6; Raipur ~800 TPD (CPCB 2020-21 estimates)
msw_total_mt.notes: Raipur dominant; moderate urbanization

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); India average for similar income level

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM Annual Report 2020-21

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: Frontiers in Agronomy 2025 (doi:10.3389/fagro.2025.1689121): Chhattisgarh total animal waste 22.4 Mt wet wt; × 0.20 DM fraction
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: ~22.4 Mt wet → ~4.5 Mt odt

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~32M pop × 24% urban × partial STP coverage; CPCB STP 2021: Chhattisgarh ~300 MLD installed capacity

nutrient_status_source: FAO/state data; ~80 kg/ha NPK; tribal rain-fed agriculture with low input use
notes: Strong forestry residue and rice straw base. Significant bamboo resource for biochar. Logistics challenging in forested areas.

name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: merged UT ~600 km² total area, ~150 km² cultivated; rice+sugarcane minor; RPR ×production ×30%
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very small UT; minor agriculture

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: DNH has ~40% forest cover (~220 km²); minimal logging; low residue
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Silvassa area has some teak plantation

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~0.6M pop × 0.70 kg/capita/day (industrial UT with high per-capita) × 365 ÷ 1e6
msw_total_mt.notes: Heavily industrialized; high per-capita waste

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); lower organic fraction in industrial UT

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM 2020-21 estimate for small industrial UTs

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: small livestock population in merged UT; 20th Livestock Census 2019

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 0.6M pop × moderate STP coverage in industrial zone

nutrient_status_source: Small agricultural area; industrial rather than agricultural UT
notes: Very small UT. Merged entity (Dadra+NH + Daman+Diu) since 2020.

name: Delhi

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ~60,000 ha agricultural land remaining (DDA land records); minor wheat/vegetable residue; 30% recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Mostly urban; peri-urban farming only

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Delhi forest/tree cover ~200 km²; urban green only; negligible extractable residue
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Urban tree pruning — minimal

msw_total_mt.source: CPCB SWM Annual Report 2020-21: Delhi ~9,457 TPD (national capital generates ~9,000-10,000 TPD); PMC9202976 Table 4: Delhi ~8,390 TPD (2015) scaled to 2020; ×365÷1e6
msw_total_mt.notes: One of India's top 2 MSW generators alongside Maharashtra. Three landfill sites (Ghazipur, Okhla, Bhalswa) — all overflowing.

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); Delhi composition surveys ~50-55% organic

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM Annual Report 2020-21; Delhi has 3 WtE plants (Timarpur-Okhla, Ghazipur, Narela-Bawana) totaling ~1,950 TPD capacity

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: 20th Livestock Census 2019 Delhi ~200,000 bovines + dairies; ×12 kg/day ×0.20 DM ×365 ÷1e6
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Urban dairy economy in peri-urban Delhi

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~20M pop × 75% STP coverage × 120 L/day × 40 mg VSS/L × 365 ÷1e9; Delhi JJM/DJB installed STP capacity ~2,715 MLD (one of highest in India, CPCB STP 2021)
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: High STP installed capacity but actual treatment ~60% of generation

nutrient_status_source: Urban UT; limited agriculture; sewage sludge nutrient-rich
notes: MSW dominates. Massive landfill crisis creates strong BiCRS via WtE/biogas incentive. High sewage sludge potential co-located with WtE infrastructure.

name: Goa

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ~0.15 Mha agricultural area (Agriculture Census); rice + cashew + coconut residue; RPR applied; 30% recoverable
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Cashew apple/shell and coconut husk significant; rice straw minor

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Goa forest ~2,200 km² (59% of state); low industrial logging; eco-tourism conservation pressure limits extraction
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot — extraction constrained

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~1.6M pop × 0.38 kg/capita/day (Goa 620 g/day highest state rate per PMC9202976, tourist-inflated × resident pop estimate) × 365 ÷ 1e6
msw_total_mt.notes: Highest per-capita MSW in India per CPCB; tourism-driven

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0; Goa higher income, lower organic fraction

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM 2020-21; Goa has WtE plant (Saligao treatment facility)

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: 20th Livestock Census 2019; small state with ~100,000 bovines; ×12 kg/day ×0.20 DM ×365 ÷1e6

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: 1.6M pop × moderate STP coverage (Panaji, Margao STPs); CPCB STP 2021 Goa ~50 MLD capacity

nutrient_status_source: FAO; small agricultural sector, low fertilizer use
notes: Tiny state. MSW dominant feedstock. Tourism waste stream adds seasonal surge.

name: Gujarat

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Hiloidhari et al. 2014; NPMCR: Gujarat gross residue ~9.63 Mt burning fraction noted (not total gross); Assessment of bioenergy generation 2021: surplus 7.6-18.3 Mt range; gross ~35 Mt (cotton+groundnut+wheat+sugarcane+rice); 30% recoverable = ~14 Mt odt
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Major crops: cotton, groundnut, sugarcane (Surat belt), wheat. Cotton stalk is significant woody residue.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Gujarat forest ~14,800 km² (7.5% of state); Gir, Dangs forests; limited commercial logging; residue factor 0.2 t/ha on accessible fraction
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Limited forest area for large state

msw_total_mt.source: PMC9202976 Table 4: Gujarat ~9,227 TPD (2015 data); scaled to 2020 ×1.15 growth; ×365÷1e6; population ~71M
msw_total_mt.notes: Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot are major generators

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); higher-income industrial state, lower organic fraction

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM Annual Report 2020-21; Gujarat among states with 60% of national STP capacity

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: Frontiers in Agronomy 2025 (doi:10.3389/fagro.2025.1689121): Gujarat total animal waste 43.3 Mt wet wt; × 0.20 DM fraction
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: ~43.3 Mt wet → ~8.7 Mt odt. Significant dairy (Amul cooperative belt).

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~71M pop × 47% urban × 55% STP coverage; Gujarat among top-5 states for installed STP capacity (CPCB STP 2021 ~3,500 MLD)
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Relatively good STP infrastructure for India

nutrient_status_source: FAO/state; ~120 kg/ha NPK; moderately intensive but below Punjab/Haryana levels
notes: Cotton stalk (woody) excellent for biochar/pyrolysis. Large manure base from dairy belt. Good industrial infrastructure for BiCRS.

name: Haryana

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Hiloidhari et al. 2014; NPMCR: surplus range 7.62-18.3 Mt (Haryana in this group); gross ~28 Mt (rice+wheat, 2 major crops); 30% recoverable = ~11 Mt odt. Haryana paddy area ~1.5 Mha, wheat ~2.5 Mha.
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: STUBBLE-BURNING HOTSPOT: ~8-10 Mt paddy straw burned annually (Oct-Nov). Punjab+Haryana together responsible for 70-80% of Delhi's winter air quality crisis from burning. Prime BiCRS opportunity — rice straw currently treated as waste.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Haryana forest ~1,600 km² (3.6% of state); largely Shivalik foothills; minimal commercial forestry
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Very limited forest cover

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~29M pop × 0.39 kg/capita/day (northern India rate) × 365 ÷ 1e6; Faridabad, Gurugram, Hisar major generators
msw_total_mt.notes: Gurugram (Gurgaon) among highest per-capita generators as Delhi satellite city

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); northern India average

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM 2020-21; Haryana has 1 WtE plant operational; top-10 state for STP capacity

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: 20th Livestock Census 2019 Haryana ~9M bovines; Haryana ScienceDirect case study: 52.29 Mt wet dung/yr; ×0.20 DM = ~10.5 Mt — cross-check: 52 Mt seems high for state population; using conservative 19 Mt wet ×0.20 = ~3.8 Mt odt based on 20th census bovine count
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Note: one ScienceDirect source cites 52.29 Mt wet dung for Haryana (high estimate); national wet dung total ~2,633 Mt with UP+Rajasthan dominant; Haryana estimate calibrated to census bovine count ~9M cattle+buffalo

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~29M pop × 35% urban × 55% STP coverage; CPCB: Haryana top-10 state STP capacity, ~700 MLD installed

nutrient_status_source: FAO fertilizer statistics 2019-20; Haryana ~200 kg/ha NPK — Green Revolution belt; one of India's highest fertilizer application rates
notes: STUBBLE-BURNING FLAG: Haryana burns ~8-10 Mt paddy straw/yr — direct conversion to BiCRS feedstock is the highest-impact intervention. Excess nutrient status favors burial/removal pathways.

name: Himachal Pradesh

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ~0.6 Mha cultivated (terraced hillside); wheat+maize+rice+apple orchards; RPR × production × 30% recoverable; apple pruning residue included
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Apple orchid pruning waste is a significant woody residue stream; wheat straw limited by terrain

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 HP forest ~15,400 km² (27.7% of state); Himalayan mixed forest; HP Forest Dept timber extraction ~1-1.5 M m³/yr; residue factor 0.3 t/m³
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: HP has active state forestry corporation; chir pine dominant species — good for biochar/pyrolysis

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~7.5M pop × 0.33 kg/capita/day × 365 ÷ 1e6; Shimla, Dharamsala main centers; tourism adds seasonal load

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018)

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM 2020-21

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: 20th Livestock Census 2019 HP ~2.5M cattle+buffalo+yak; 10 kg/head/day (hill cattle smaller) ×0.20 DM ×365 ÷1e6
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Mountain cattle and yak; stall-fed cattle manure collectible

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~7.5M pop × 12% urban × partial STP coverage; CPCB STP 2021 HP limited capacity ~50 MLD

nutrient_status_source: FAO; mountain/hill state, ~60 kg/ha NPK; terraced subsistence agriculture
notes: Terrain limits feedstock aggregation. Forest and apple orchard residues are best BiCRS opportunities.

name: Jammu and Kashmir

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ~0.8 Mha cultivated (J&K UT post-bifurcation); rice+wheat+maize+fruit orchards; RPR × production × 30% recoverable; burning rate >30% noted in NPMCR
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Apple and other fruit orchard pruning residue is economically significant. Rice straw burning prevalent.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: J&K UT (excl. Ladakh) forest area ~20,000 km²; J&K Forest Dept operations; deodar/fir/pine harvesting; residue factor 0.3 t accessible/ha
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Significant coniferous forest; Deodar cedar valued timber

msw_total_mt.source: calc: J&K UT ~15M pop × 0.30 kg/capita/day × 365 ÷ 1e6; Srinagar ~450 TPD, Jammu ~350 TPD (CPCB estimates)
msw_total_mt.notes: J&K UT (post-2019 bifurcation from Ladakh)

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018)

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM 2020-21

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: calc: 20th Livestock Census 2019 J&K ~4.5M bovines+sheep+goat; mixed livestock; 8 kg/head eq/day ×0.20 DM ×365 ÷1e6
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: Sheep/goat dominant in Kashmir Valley; cattle in Jammu

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~15M pop × 30% urban × limited STP coverage; conflict-affected infrastructure
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Limited functional STP capacity

nutrient_status_source: FAO; ~100 kg/ha NPK; fruit-orchard intensive fertilization in Kashmir valley
notes: J&K UT (excludes Ladakh since 2019). Crop residue burning >30% flagged. Orchard pruning waste is underutilized.

name: Jharkhand

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: NPMCR: Jharkhand ~1.90 Mt gross burned (high burn fraction >30%); gross total estimated ~8 Mt; 30% recoverable = ~3.2 Mt odt
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Rice dominant; tribal subsistence farming. High burning rate noted in NPMCR (>30% burned).

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Jharkhand forest ~23,400 km² (29% of state); Sal dominated; moderate logging/charcoal production; residue factor 0.3 t/ha on ~20% accessible
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Significant Sal and bamboo forest; charcoal burning traditional use

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~38M pop × 0.22 kg/capita/day × 365 ÷ 1e6; low urbanization ~24%; Ranchi, Jamshedpur major centers

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); low-income state, high organic fraction

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM 2020-21

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: Frontiers in Agronomy 2025 (doi:10.3389/fagro.2025.1689121): Jharkhand total animal waste 26.5 Mt wet wt; × 0.20 DM fraction
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: ~26.5 Mt wet → ~5.3 Mt odt

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~38M pop × 24% urban × limited STP coverage; Ranchi STP dominant

nutrient_status_source: FAO/state data; tribal rain-fed agriculture, low external input use; acidic lateritic soils
notes: High crop residue burning rate (>30%). Forest and manure feedstocks strong. Mining-belt industrial waste also present.

name: Karnataka

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Hiloidhari et al. 2014; NPMCR: Karnataka ~5.82 Mt burned (high burn fraction); Assessment 2021: surplus 7.62-18.3 Mt; gross ~34 Mt (sugarcane+rice+maize+jowar+ragi+cotton); 30% recoverable = ~13.5 Mt
ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Major crops: sugarcane (Mandya belt), rice, cotton, maize, ragi. Cotton stalk and sugarcane tops are key BiCRS feedstocks. NPMCR notes Karnataka burns more than generates for selected crops — reflects residue classification methodology.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Karnataka forest ~37,600 km² (19.6% of state); Western Ghats (Kodagu) + Malnad region; some commercial timber (Eucalyptus, Acacia); residue factor 0.3 t/ha on 15% accessible
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: Western Ghats biodiversity hotspot limits extraction; Eucalyptus plantations in Malnad add harvestable residue

msw_total_mt.source: PMC9202976 Table 4: Karnataka ~8,784 TPD (2015 data); scaled to 2020 ×1.15; ×365÷1e6; Bengaluru alone ~5,000 TPD
msw_total_mt.notes: Bengaluru (Bangalore) is India's 3rd-largest MSW generator

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018); Bengaluru composition studies ~55%

msw_treatment.source: CPCB SWM 2020-21; Karnataka (esp. BBMP Bengaluru) has advanced dry waste collection and composting programs

animal_manure_odt_mt.source: Frontiers in Agronomy 2025 (doi:10.3389/fagro.2025.1689121): Karnataka total animal waste 26.6 Mt wet wt; × 0.20 DM fraction
animal_manure_odt_mt.notes: ~26.6 Mt wet → ~5.3 Mt odt

human_wwtp_odt_mt.source: calc: ~68M pop × 39% urban × 55% STP coverage; Karnataka/Bengaluru among top-5 for installed STP capacity (CPCB STP 2021 ~2,000 MLD)
human_wwtp_odt_mt.notes: Bengaluru large STP network

nutrient_status_source: FAO; ~115 kg/ha NPK; moderate Green Revolution adoption, rainfed agriculture dominant in north Karnataka

name: Kerala

ag_residues_odt_mt.notes: Coconut shell/husk and rubber wood (replanting cycle ~25-30 yr) are key woody residues. Rice area declining. Rubber wood excellent biochar feedstock.

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 Kerala forest ~21,100 km² (54% of state); Western Ghats strict protection; limited logging; rubber plantation timber residue substantial (private land); residue factor 0.2 t/ha on accessible fringe + private rubber

notes: Rubber wood and coconut shell are premium biochar feedstocks. Kerala's organized municipalities make MSW more collectible than average.

name: Madhya Pradesh

ag_residues_odt_mt.source: Hiloidhari et al. 2014; Assessment 2021: surplus 7.62-18.3 Mt for MP; NPMCR: MP gross ~3.86 Mt burned only; gross total ~41 Mt (wheat+soybean+rice+jowar+maize+pulses); 30% recoverable = ~16.5 Mt odt

forestry_residues_odt_mt.source: calc: ISFR 2021 MP forest area 77,493 km² (2nd largest after Arunachal Pradesh); MPFDC active; Teak/Sal extraction; residue factor 0.3 t/ha on 15% accessible area (11,600 km²); plus bamboo
forestry_residues_odt_mt.notes: 2nd highest forest area nationally. Significant bamboo (bioenergy+biochar potential). Tendu leaf collection economy. Some paper mills (Raipur/Hoshangabad belt).

msw_total_mt.source: calc: ~87M pop × 0.30 kg/capita/day × 365 ÷ 1e6; Indore, Bhopal, Jabalpur major generators; Indore ranked #1 cleanest city in India (Swachh Survekshan)
msw_total_mt.notes: Indore has model waste management with door-to-door collection and segregation

msw_biogenic_frac.source: World Bank What a Waste 2.0 (2018)
